name: Hamish Mann
life: “I still remember moving a chair closer in a room full of strangers.” Saturday often includes a stop at Juniper Street, where Hamish knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I had planned to wait outside. Seeing the lender sit alone made me move one chair closer.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a red windbreaker and a replacement button a shade darker than the others. Hamish has a long face and high cheekbones, with a center part and straight chestnut hair. Hamish looks toward the door whenever a name is called during a conversation.
personality: Hamish has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To offer the lender quiet company inside.
family: Kathleen Roy is Hamish’s cousin. Hamish gets to change the plan. Kathleen offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The uniform money*, Kathleen says, “I earned the uniform money washing hotel sheets.”
connections: Magdalena Zhang. Someone sitting beside the lender and the person returning his coat can spare him a solitary wait.

reactions.situation: A stranger asks why the lender came to court
reactions.response: Hamish lets the lender tell or withhold the coat's history.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Hamish stays where both neighbors can hear a familiar voice and gets news from the caretaker.

reactions.situation: When a private quarrel becomes a public joke
reactions.response: Hamish says the plainest truthful thing possible and changes the subject.
